title: Microsoft Copilot Chat: Tools menu in the prompt box
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, Copilot Chat requirements and Integrated Apps blocking path are supported. Searches found no separate control, licence or meter for the Tools menu itself, and the briefing reports the conflicting Microsoft guidance about blocking scope and Teams.

claims.claim: A Tools-menu-specific rollout sequence and which users or tenants receive it first are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat Tools Control 497298 administrator action rollout menu; Copilot Chat Tools menu default rollout. Read roadmap, release notes, Manage agents and Researcher FAQ; no menu-specific first-wave audience or sequence found.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat Tools Control 497298 administrator action rollout menu. Read Manage Copilot Chat, Configure Microsoft Copilot settings, Manage agents and release notes; no menu-specific administrator action found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn names Researcher and Analyst under Tools without giving an exhaustive list of the menu's entries.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat Tools Control 497298 administrator action rollout menu. Read roadmap, Manage agents, Researcher FAQ and release notes; found a user-selected entry point, not a statement of unattended changes to existing features.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Copilot features generally as gradually rolling out to a subset of users in a tenant before expanding across the organisation.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.claim: Roles that configure the Tools menu itself are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat Tools menu default rollout administrator setting permissions. Read Configure Microsoft Copilot settings, Manage agents, Manage Copilot Chat and Integrated Apps; documented roles concern other settings, not a Tools-menu configuration control.

claims.claim: The Copilot app blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. ... Select Block app.

claims.claim: Automation equivalent to blocking the Copilot Chat host app through Integrated Apps is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Integrated Apps block Copilot app PowerShell Microsoft Graph API block app; "Copilot app" "Integrated" "PowerShell" block. Read Integrated Apps, Manage Copilot Chat and copilotPackage block reference excerpt; package blocking does not document host-app blocking.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI or API switch for the Tools menu itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat Tools menu default rollout administrator setting permissions; Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat Tools Control 497298 administrator action rollout menu. Read Configure Microsoft Copilot settings, Manage Copilot Chat, Manage agents and Integrated Apps; no menu switch.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps withdraws access to the app that provides Copilot Chat on web and desktop.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page says these controls are only available to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page says Teams retains its own settings in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center

claims.claim: Integrated Apps CoPilot settings apply to Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat as whole apps, rather than to the Tools menu alone.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page says blocking an app blocks it for all users in the organisation.
claims.quote: When you choose to block an app, it is blocked for all users in your organization. Blocking an app overrides any previous admin deployment or user installation in Microsoft 365 and Outlook

claims.claim: In contrast to the Integrated Apps page, Manage Copilot Chat describes blocking as tenant-wide and scopeable to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.

claims.claim: In contrast to the Integrated Apps page, Manage Copilot Chat says its Integrated Apps block also blocks Copilot in Teams.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.claim: Restricting app availability is not equivalent to blocking because availability settings do not affect admin-deployed apps.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own.

controlChecks.governs: Whether users can use Copilot Chat, the app that hosts the Tools menu
